result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A labels each problem with a severity, gives an explicit fix order and has a 'What to keep' section that praises the cream background, the serif type and the specific copy. B finds most of the same problems but gives no per-item severity and says nothing about what already works. B's fixes are a near-complete CSS rewrite rather than ordered, targeted changes, and its estimate of about 150 characters per line looks too high. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B labels each problem with a severity, gives a clear fix order with specific values (#595959, 40–48px h1, 640px measure, 44px targets) and names several things worth keeping. A covers the same main problems with the same values and adds useful CSS, but it only loosely ranks the problems and never says what already works. B's choice to rank the broken links above the visual problems is defensible, and it still names the inverted hierarchy as the main reason the page feels off.
